A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TR-DRL research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-control simulation experiments on Robosuite and Meta-World, including learning curves, numerical comparisons, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results in Section 5 and the appendices, including success rates and training episodes required to reach success.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same inverse and forward dynamics models, reversal filtering, potential-based reward shaping, and training procedure. The MOORE implementation mentioned in v2 does not specify a revised TR-DRL procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 10 Robosuite environments and 50 Meta-World MT50 tasks, identifying the same 12 reversible task pairs within MT50. No new evaluated domain or test scenario is reported.

E2.justification: The single-task, task-conditioned, multi-headed, and language-conditioned SAC comparison sets remain unchanged in their corresponding experiments. v2 mentions a MOORE-based code implementation, but supplies no evaluated MOORE comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain sparse rewards, initialization with 10 demonstration trajectories, and evaluation every 20 training episodes using 20 evaluation episodes. Table 1 is identical. The corrected filtering-threshold legend matches values already specified in v1 Appendix F, rather than introducing a new protocol.

E4.justification: The filtering ablation, threshold sensitivity study, potential-model training comparisons, and potential-labeling-function study are retained. v2 Appendix E separates existing comparisons into additional plots; it introduces no new analytical question or experimental evidence.

E5.justification: v2 checklist item 7 newly states that aggregate IQM performance has 95% confidence intervals. Both versions retain five-run reporting and standard-deviation descriptions. This adds uncertainty-reporting information without establishing additional runs or a new estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Figures 4-6 and Tables 2-3 are unchanged, as are the retained learning curves. For example, Table 2's aggregate language-conditioned TR-SAC result remains 140±25 episodes. New Figures 18-19 redisplay existing results; Figure 16 changes legend labels without changing its curves.

T1.justification: The full and partial time-reversal definitions, mathematical objectives, and potential-based shaping formulation remain unchanged. SAC background moves from v1 Appendix B into v2 Section 3; equation renumbering and an explanation of reversal notation introduce no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: partial time-reversal symmetry, two complementary techniques, and improved sample efficiency and performance on the same benchmarks. The abstract's added project and code information does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix M explicitly adds dependence on prior knowledge of task structure, specifically time-reversal symmetry, as a limitation. The existing simulation-only limitation and interpretations of the experimental findings remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page and source-code access information and states in Appendix B that the code includes an implementation built upon MOORE. Hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures are otherwise retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the external repository's contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning action persistence, state decomposition, noise robustness, symmetric behavior learning, and MOORE, including Hu et al. (2024b), Pitis et al. (2020), Yao et al. (2023), and Hendawy et al. (2024). These modestly extend contextualization without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 moves the additional related work and SAC background from v1 Appendices A-B into Sections 2-3, removes duplicated reset-policy discussion, and adds acknowledgments and a conference checklist. Front matter and cross-references are updated, while most research prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 18-19 with separate plots for method pairs already combined in Figures 5-6. Figure 16 corrects the peg-panel legends from repeated beta=0.01 labels to 0.01, 0.001, and 0.0001. Caption edits and relocated figures and tables accompany these limited presentation improvements.

improvement.justification: v2 makes existing evidence easier to interpret through separate comparison plots and corrected threshold legends, adds explicit code-access information, and acknowledges dependence on known task symmetry. These improve usability and transparency. The underlying method and empirical validation are unchanged, and the new confidence-interval statement does not explain its estimation procedure, so the overall gain is limited.
